agent_notes: Another crux. Verbs נִשְׁמְטוּ (perfect) and וְשָׁמְעוּ (converted perfect) are both read in the dramatic layer as future/imprecatory, as Radak and Meiri allow; the literal layer keeps the perfect for the first. The meaning of 'at the hands of the rock' (בִּידֵי־סֶלַע) is uncertain: 'by the sides of a cliff' (ASV), 'into the power of the rock', or 'at the hands of the Rock' (God). I keep 'hands' in the literal layer and flag the options.

The KJV 'grave's mouth' for לְפִי שְׁאוֹל is fine; its 'as when one cutteth and cleaveth wood' adds the word 'wood', which is not in the Hebrew (Rashi supplies עֵצִים, so does Radak implicitly). YLT 'at the command of Saul' is a mistaken confusion of שְׁאוֹל with שָׁאוּל. I gloss פֹלֵחַ/בֹקֵעַ as 'one who plows' and 'one who splits' in the literal text, keeping 'earth' ambiguous between plowing and splitting wood on the ground.
